tagline: From a creek-powered mill up to a wall of uncertain age.
intro: The byway starts at Prater's Mill on Coahulla Creek in Whitfield County and follows State Route 2 past pasture into Murray County, then US 41 and quiet county roads into the Chattahoochee National Forest. It skirts Chatsworth and takes State Route 52 up into the Cohutta Mountains. The climb runs from around 800 feet to above 2,500, past Fort Mountain State Park to an overlook at the top.
Spurs run off to the Cohutta Fish Hatchery and to a Forest Service camp on Holly Creek, the stream that runs down the east edge of Chatsworth.

moments.title: Prater's Mill
moments.text: Coahulla Creek ran the machinery here, and for almost a hundred years farmers lined up early with their mules and wagons to wait their turn with the millers.

moments.title: Chatsworth
moments.text: The town began in 1905 as a railroad depot, and the story goes that it took its name from a sign that fell off a passing freight train.

moments.title: Fort Mountain State Park
moments.text: On the peak a zigzag wall of local stone runs along the summit, and a 1956 archaeological report declined to guess how old it is.
